findings.title: Existing RECREATE exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes 4. The command's exit code is a documented contract for CI/CD scripts (the update-compatibility guide tells users to branch on it). Any pipeline that treats 4 as 'rolling upgrade not possible' will now misread a feature-disabled condition as a recreate requirement, and the old value now means something else. The change is only justified if the old code 4 was never released; the PR does not state this, and the new code should be checked against the released behaviour.

findings.title: Null-strategy deployments never enable rolling-updates, but the operator now requires it
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, before the FeatureSpec with rolling-updates is set. The PR's own docs say the operator fails when rolling-updates is not enabled. The null-strategy case of testCacheMaxCount expects eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus, so that test will run against an operator with the feature disabled and fail or behave incorrectly. The feature enablement must happen for every case, not only after the early return.

findings.title: Feature setup overwrites any existing enabled features
findings.body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) replaces the whole enabled list rather than appending to it. If getTestKeycloakDeployment or a future caller sets other enabled features, they are silently dropped. Merge the lists instead.

findings.title: Feature gate runs before config validation and depends on Profile being initialised
findings.body: Profile.isFeatureEnabled dereferences Profile.getInstance() and unboxes features.get(feature). If Profile has not been configured, or the feature key is absent from the map, this throws a NullPointerException instead of a clean CLI error. Nothing in the PR guarantees Profile is initialised before run() is reached.
